definitions.explanation: A vision condition in which distant objects can be seen more clearly than nearby objects.

examples.japanese: {遠視|えんし}⟦で→で：00502_de⟧{近|ちか}く⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{文字|もじ}→文字：03632_moji⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{読|よ}み→読む：00426_yomu⟧にくい。
examples.english: I have farsightedness, so it's hard to read text up close.

examples.japanese: {遠視用|えんしよう}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{眼鏡|めがね}をかけている→眼鏡をかける：20967_meganewokakeru⟧。
{子|こ}ども⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{遠視|えんし}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{早|はや}め→早め：11176_hayame⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{治療|ちりょう}→治療：03503_chiryou⟧⟦した→する：00392_suru⟧⟦ほうがいい→ほうがいい：10078_hougaii⟧。
examples.english: It's better to treat farsightedness in children early.

notes:
CONTRAST WITH OTHER VISION CONDITIONS:
- ⟦{近視|きんし}→近視：02683_kinshi⟧ (nearsightedness/myopia - difficulty seeing far)
- ⟦{老眼|ろうがん}→老眼：06369_rougan⟧ (presbyopia - age-related farsightedness)
- ⟦{乱視|らんし}→乱視：06370_ranshi⟧ (astigmatism)

NOTE ON {遠視|えんし} vs ⟦{老眼|ろうがん}→老眼：06369_rougan⟧:
{遠視|えんし} is a refractive error that can occur at any age, where the eye focuses light behind the retina. ⟦{老眼|ろうがん}→老眼：06369_rougan⟧ is the natural loss of near-focusing ability that occurs with aging, typically starting around age 40.
